note: Every print sample was filmed on a phone in the shop, so each one showed a wall, a counter or a stranger standing next to the press. The owner asked for the print and the packaging, nothing else. This is the per-clip crop that answers that, chosen frame by frame from /tmp/bh-audio/sheet_*.jpg contact sheets. tools/clipfit.swift cut <src> <dst> <x> <y> <w> <h> bed <maxKb*1024> is the tool that made these files; tests/catalog-clips.test.mjs holds the shipped clips to this plan.
dur: seconds of picture the visitor actually gets, read back out of the shipped file
t0/t1: seconds of the SOURCE a clip was cut down to, when no crop of the whole take could drop the person standing in it
x: pixels from the LEFT edge of the unbaked source frame
y: pixels from the TOP edge of the unbaked source frame
maxKb: never heavier than the clip it replaces
sound: "bed" in each row below means the clip carries the site bed rather than its own camera audio. As of 2026-11-16 that bed is the owner's own recording: he sent a 26.0s phone take of the press and asked for its sound on every clip, so tools/clipfit swap <src> <dst> <sound-src> re-laid all 35 with it. It normalises the take to -23 dBFS and takes it whole for a clip shorter than 26.0s; the 14 clips that outlive the take loop it, and a loop is only worth having if the seam is invisible — the joins sit inside the take's own quiet trough (2.00-25.33s) and crossfade over 0.35s at equal power, because butt-jointing its loud opening onto its quiet tail is a splice you hear. Measured off the shipped 47.3s clip: spread 75.3 dB, rms -23.0 dBFS, clip 0, dominant partial 58 Hz. Same figures as his file (spread 73.6, rms -22.8), and that clip's eleven band readings match it to the decibel (40:-8 58:-1 100:-12 150:-20 250:-29 400:-31 800:-30 1500:-52 3000:-43 6000:-44 12000:-42), which is what looping a recording without colouring it looks like; the synthesised tone this replaced measured spread 10.2 with a -118 dB top octave. That tone has its own history worth keeping: it took two passes to stop it sounding like rain — first the generated noise wash went, then the motion went (two partial pairs 3.5 Hz and 17 Hz apart, a 41 Hz sub, a 0.8 Hz phase wobble and a 10 dB drip-shaped press pulse), because a low drone that wobbles reads as water on a tin roof even when its spectrum measures clean. What it ended as — one exact 58 Hz harmonic stack pulsing 3 dB on the 1.9 Hz press cycle — is why the owner's own press recording was acceptable as its replacement: the partials agree. The picture never moves. swap copies the compressed samples straight through, so not one cropped frame shifted (proved per file by an identical video stsz table), and every row's x/y/w/h/dur below still describes the file on disk. His recording is broadband and the tone was not, so it costs bytes: 113,503 KB → 116,849 KB across the 35 (+2.9%), because swap encodes the audio at 128 kbps where the crop pass encoded a pure tone at about 44 kbps. Every clip still sits inside the maxKb its row sets, which is what that column guards.
